prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hours; protection overrides regulation. Operations Control Centre’s Line Traffic Controller monitors operations, records incidents/first-safe-instruction, assesses passenger/downstream impacts, owns regulation/recovery decisions, issues confirmed Temporary Speed Restriction Notice, verifies revised timetable visibility. Authority reviews after major-incidents/degraded-operations/timetable-interventions check interlocking-state/controller-intent/recorded-response consistency. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; displays proposed regulation/action/trains/recovery before confirmation; commanded/locked routes/points/occupancy separately. Revenue Train Operator reports condition/cab-indications/passengers/local-hazards; repeats Voice Dispatch Console instructions before acceptance; voice never substitutes safety-data. Field staff support fallback. Signal Maintenance Engineer(Maple) records clearance before restoration, advises equipment recovery. Maintenance Diagnostic Server(Quarry) supplies non-vital diagnostics/trends for equipment-versus-operational causation; no vital decisions/bypass. Service Timetable Server: approved-change-workflow only. Passenger Information Gateway receives operational service state aligning platform-messages/train-destinations; schedules/information isolated/non-vital. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supplies onboard/path-authentication material, checks sample-report certificate-windows/controller-clock tolerance before use, produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack during approved maintenance-window, records audit-reference; no safety-logic changes. Cyber Security Officer reviews certificate-changes/access-events/unusual-authentication-failures before renewed-security operational approval. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid): validated authorities/separation/locking/conflict-reports. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking: vital points/routes/releases; indications to zones/onboard. Authorities require consistent approaches/protection/proved-detected-locked points; lost correspondence restricts. East sends Axle Counter Reset Request; no reset with locked-routes/approaching-trains. West sends Route Release Exception List; retain hazards until excluded. Independent axle-count occupancy; conflicting-locations restrictive. Transfers require odometer-confirmed position/receiving-zone validation/reissue. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): authenticated power/integrity/token-context; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train-operation/fallback/cutout; validates/enforces authorities/speed/doors/commands/profiles; cyclewise braking; rejection/degradation reports; Brake Curve Checksum Log. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot per monitored

New part:
S133: Station status indications presented to local station staff are derived from validated CBTC states rather than from unverified field contacts alone.
S134: These indications distinguish normal service, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop active, and evacuation support conditions.
S135: The Metro Operations Control System displays station and platform states with the same identifiers used in controller workstations to reduce interpretation errors during incidents.
S136: Passenger Information Gateway receives train prediction data, stopping pattern changes, and platform allocation updates after the CBTC system has reconciled them with the active timetable.
S137: The Passenger Information Gateway shall not publish a revised destination or skip-stop message until the underlying train identity and route have been confirmed by the CBTC system.
S138: When a platform is taken out of service, the passenger information interface marks the affected train movements as unavailable for boarding while retaining their operational tracking in the control center.
S139: Service Timetable Server provides planned service context used to compare predicted arrivals against scheduled platform usage.
S140: Metro Operations Control System coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, and station crowding information before it is released to passenger-facing systems.
S141: Voice Dispatch Console displays train calling identity, current platform association, and the latest operational hold reason so that spoken instructions match automated indications.
S142: The Line Traffic Controller may apply a station hold through dispatch controls, and the hold is reflected in CBTC departure logic without changing the underlying route locking rules.
S143: Dispatch-related controls use positive confirmation and cancellation states so that a cancelled hold is not confused with a timeout, failed message, or rejected command.
S144: Kestrel shall report train door enable side, berth identity, and departure readiness to support platform interface checks during dwell and dispatch.
S145: Saffron shall maintain message delivery paths for station interface traffic during normal radio coverage transitions and degraded coverage recovery.
S146: Train Radio Modem uses the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before accepting renewed secure sessions for passenger-facing and station-interface data paths.
S147: Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-relevant station interface messages separately from nonvital passenger information messages.
S148: Maintenance Diagnostic Server records station interface faults, rejected commands, and inconsistent indications for later investigation by the Signal Maintenance Engineer.
S149: Cyber Security Officer reviews access rights for passenger information and dispatch integration workstations when station-facing interfaces are commissioned or materially changed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
